concepts.def: Shift from high birth and death rates to low rates as societies industrialise.
Maximum population an environment can sustainably support.
Thomas Malthus (1798) argued population grows faster than food supply, causing crises.
Area of productive land needed to sustain a person's consumption and absorb their waste.
Faster use of non-renewables (minerals, fossil fuels) than they form or can be substituted.
Bar chart by age and sex; shape reveals demographic stage and future trends.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Biological Resources — a core area of A-Level Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Biological Resources brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Biological Resources.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
